Article Title: Moody’s chief economist Mark Zandi sees 'big warning' signs in June Jobs report for the US; says: Decline in unemployment rate was misleading because it coincided with a sharp drop in ...
Article Text:
Household survey weakness



Adjusted unemployment measure



Other economists weigh in



Mark Zandi, the chief economist of Moody’s Analytics has cautioned that the June employment report paints an overly optimistic picture of the US labour market. According to a report by Benzinga, in a series of posts shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Zandi argued that commentary around the report was “much too dismissive of how weak the numbers looked, all the noise in the data notwithstanding. ” Zandi noted that payroll employment posted only modest gain in June, while in the months prior to June, job gains were revised downward. He further added that most of the hiring came from the healthcare sector rather than being broadly distributed across the economy.“Not only did employment as measured by the payroll survey post a small gain in the month, but previous month’s gains were revised much lower, and the bulk of the job gains were in healthcare. And employment as measured by the household survey fell sharply again, as it has all year,” wrote Zandi.The economist further pointed to the household survey, saying employment “fell sharply again, as it has all year.” He argued that the decline in the rate of unemployment was misleading because it coincided with a sharp drop in labour force participation. Participation has fallen across most demographic groups, particularly among workers under 35.“The unemployment rate ticked lower, but only because labor force participation is in free-fall. Participation is down across most demographic groups, especially among workers under 35. Employment-to-population ratio for prime-age workers also fell. The declines are surely overstated, but even so,” added Zandi.Zandi cited his “vicious-cycle measure,” which adjusts unemployment for trend labor force participation. He said the measure rose above 5% in June: “Without the outsize decline in participation, unemployment would be over 5%.”“You may recall our vicious-cycle measure, which adjusts the unemployment rate for trend labor force participation. It rose to over 5% in June. That is, without the outsize decline in participation, unemployment would be over 5%. As I said, the commentary on the June report was much too sanguine,” wrote Zandi in a post on X.Some economists echoed concerns about the June data. Laura Ullrich of Indeed Hiring Lab suggested the decline in participation may reflect a shrinking worker supply rather than weaker hiring demand, noting employers could still be seeking workers but facing fewer available candidates.Meanwhile, Cathie Wood of ARK Invest called the report “weird”, arguing government labor statistics appeared distorted due to differences between payroll and household surveys. She advocated using more private-sector data to assess labor market conditions.
Article Summary: Mark Zandi, the chief economist of Moody’s Analytics has cautioned that the June employment report paints an overly optimistic picture of the US labour market. Zandi argued that commentary around the report was “much too dismissive of how weak the numbers looked, all the noise in the data notwithstanding”

Article Title: How the massive luxury Superyacht of Russia's richest man used ‘vanishing tech’ while crossing the Strait of Hormuz, resurfacing 5,050 miles away in Bali
Article Text:
The ‘vanishing tech’



Nord: What makes this yacht different



An enormous, 465-foot (142-metre) luxury superyacht linked to a Russian billionaire reappeared in Bali, Indonesia, after pulling off a ‘high-tech vanishing act’ in one of the world's most dangerous maritime chokepoints. The vessel, named Nord, was spotted docked at the commercial harbor in Benoa, Bali. What makes Nord’s arrival in Bali particularly mysterious is how it got there. At a time when intense geopolitical conflicts have left many commercial shipping vessels stranded or terrified to enter the Strait of Hormuz, the massive superyacht casually cruised right through the waterway.According to the tracking data, the vessel was spotted around the Strait of Hormuz in late April and disappeared – crossing vast oceans starting from Dubai and landing in Indonesia. The six-deck explorer yacht has covered roughly 4,400 nautical miles (around 5,050 miles) across the Indian Ocean.Shortly after passing through the strait, Nord effectively went invisible. The ship’s crew reportedly turned off its AIS (Automatic Identification System) transponder, a standard marine safety device or equipment that combines GPS and radio transmitters to continuously broadcast a ship's identity, location, speed and direction to avoid collisions.By cutting the feed, the yacht went completely dark to public tracking systems. It managed to slip across the ocean entirely unseen, only to suddenly pop back up on tracking data and Instagram videos once it safely arrived in Bali, as per publication Luxurylaunches.Standing at 10,154 gross tons, Nord is too gigantic to hide, even when it tries to turn off its tracking tech. In fact, the vessel is so massive that it could not even fit inside Bali's luxury Benoa Marina, hence, it was forced to dock at the commercial harbor alongside the towering cargo vessels and cruise ships that normally dominate the waterfront. While docked, the crew refueled the yacht’s 345,000-liter fuel tanks.Delivered in 2021 by the renowned German shipyard Lürssen, Nord is widely recognised as one of the most advanced private explorer yachts on the planet. Far more than a simple pleasure cruiser, it is built to survive massive ocean voyages.The floating palace can host up to 36 guests across 20 ultra-luxury cabins and requires a crew of more than 40 people to run. It has two functional helipads; a private swimming pool, spa and fitness gym; cinema room, a custom built-in submarine and a massive collection of water toys.The vessel is widely linked to Russian steel magnate and billionaire Alexey Mordashov, the primary shareholder of Severstal. The yacht is valued at an estimated $500 million.Keeping a ship of this scale operational requires an astronomical amount of cash. Running a superyacht reportedly costs about 10% of the vessel's total value annually, which means that Mordashov could be spending up to $50 million a year on the maintenance, crew and fuel needed to keep Nord moving.
Article Summary: The 465-foot (142-metre) luxury superyacht reappeared in Bali, Indonesia, after pulling off a ‘high-tech vanishing act’ in one of the world's most dangerous maritime chokepoints. The vessel, named Nord, was spotted docked at the commercial harbor in Benoa, Bali. Nord is widely linked to Russian steel magnate and billionaire Alexey Mordashov, the primary shareholder of Severstal.

Article Title: Larry Ellison and David Larry Ellison sued by Paramount investors for 'government connection'; lawsuit claims promise to fire anchors Trump does not like, settle ...
Article Text:
Allegations of ‘remaking’ networks



Paramount fires back: ‘Recycled allegations’



Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) merger is facing legal hurdle. A shareholder lawsuit has been filed against tech billionaire Larry Ellison and his son, Paramount Skydance Chief David Ellison , accusing them of striking a corrupt, ‘illegal’ backroom deal with President Donald Trump to clear regulatory hurdles for a historic media merger, a report has said. The lawsuit, filed by Paramount stockholder Paul Robbins in the Delaware Chancery Court, seeks to completely block Paramount’s massive $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD).Citing the complaint, a report by Variety says that lawsuit alleges the Ellisons promised “illegal private benefits to President Trump” in exchange for the White House smoothing over federal antitrust barriers. According to the suit, this secret agreement included an opportunity to funnel cash to the president by settling his ongoing legal claims against CNN. Furthermore, the Ellisons reportedly promised that CNN anchors whom Trump dislikes would be fired immediately after the takeover.The lawsuit further claims that the Ellisons’ political maneuvering has already damaged the media properties they control. Following the initial August 2025 merger between Skydance and Paramount Global, the suit alleges the Ellisons quickly “proceeded to remake CBS in the president’s image, bought properties he enjoyed, and even hosted events to honor him.”Shareholders argue these moves have alienated audiences, causing networks to “hemorrhage viewers.” The lawsuit also highlights a series of unusual regulatory green lights as evidence of a quid pro quo. In mid-June, the US Justice Department officially cleared the Paramount-WBD acquisition without demanding a single corporate divestiture or concession.Furthermore, the suit points out that federal regulators have taken a conspicuously hands-off approach ever since Trump publicly indicated his preference for Paramount to buy WBD over a competing bid from Netflix.The legal challenge arrived a day after 12 Democratic state attorneys general filed a federal lawsuit to block the deal on antitrust grounds, arguing the combined entity would hold an illegal monopoly over theatrical and cable TV markets. The Writers Guild of America (WGA) has also sued, claiming the consolidation will depress writers' pay and eliminate jobs.Paramount has vehemently denied the explosive claims, pushing back against the lawsuit’s narrative.“This lawsuit recycles allegations that have already been reported and already addressed. No commitments from either David or Larry Ellison have been made to any government body, State AG, or federal agency regarding the future of CNN or any other news property, other than the goal to deliver truth-based journalism,” a Paramount spokesperson stated.The company added that the merger stands entirely on its own economic merits, promising it will give consumers more choices and increase investment in original programming.
Article Summary: Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) merger is facing legal hurdle. A shareholder lawsuit has been filed against tech billionaire Larry Ellison and his son, Paramount Skydance Chief David Ellison. The suit alleges the Ellisons promised ‘illegal private benefits to President Trump’ in exchange for the White House smoothing over federal antitrust barriers.

Article Title: Why Korea's AI-powered baseball umpires are making life harder for the league's biggest stars
Article Text:
Representative Image

Study links ABS system to changes in strike-zone decisions



“This suggests that there may have been an existing bias in favour of prominent batters before ABS,”

“Before ABS, when a big-name batter was at bat, umpires may have given more favourable calls on borderline pitches.”

Researchers say findings extend beyond baseball



“We’ve all seen calls that have influenced outcomes at the end of the game,”

“Some decisions made by officials, like ball-strike decisions or out-of-bounds calls, are very objective and could be automated easily.”

“Human judgment, in my view, remains useful for more subjective decisions, and for that reason I do not believe we will see human officiating go away completely anytime soon,”

The introduction of robotic ball-strike calls in South Korea's professional baseball league has reportedly coincided with a decline in the performance of some of the league's top hitters. According to a new study, researchers found that after the Korea Baseball Organisation (KBO) adopted its Automatic Ball-Strike (ABS) system in the 2024 season, high-profile batters received fewer favourable outcomes on borderline pitches compared to the previous year.The findings, published in the journal European Sport Management Quarterly, suggest that prominent batters walked less, struck out more and reached base less often after the AI-assisted system was introduced. The researchers said the results suggest that well-known players may have benefited from favourable strike-zone decisions before the technology was adopted.The KBO introduced the ABS system in 2024 to assist home plate umpires with ball-and-strike decisions. Rather than replacing umpires, the system uses pitch-tracking sensors and camera arrays to determine whether a pitch crosses the strike zone, with the analysis relayed to the human umpire, who then announces the call.Researchers from the University of Michigan compared player performance before and after the introduction of ABS and found that the statistical decline was concentrated in areas related to strike-zone judgment rather than overall hitting ability.Jimin Song, a University of Michigan kinesiologist and study co-author, said in a statement.The researchers noted that while star hitters experienced changes in walk rate, strikeouts and on-base performance, broader hitting statistics showed less noticeable differences. According to the study, this supports the view that the change was linked to strike-zone calls rather than a decline in players' batting ability.The same trend was not observed among prominent pitchers. The researchers said this could be due to greater variation in pitching performance or fewer opportunities to detect a similar pattern.The researchers said the results highlight how technology can reduce bias in objective decisions. They added that the implications may extend to other settings where human judgment can be influenced by an individual's status.said study co-author and University of Michigan kinesiologist Richard Paulsen.The study also noted that status bias can occur in workplaces, educational institutions, and other environments characterised by unequal power dynamics. The researchers suggested approaches such as blind performance reviews and evaluations as ways to reduce such bias.Despite the widespread use of automated ball-strike technology, including Major League Baseball testing, the researchers do not expect it to replace officials entirely.said Paulsen.
Article Summary: Study links ABS system to changes in strike-zone decisions in South Korea. High- profile batters received fewer favourable outcomes on borderline pitches after the system was introduced in 2024. Researchers said results highlight how technology can reduce bias in objective decisions. They added that the implications may extend to other settings where human judgment can be influenced by an individual's status.

Article Title: IRCTC launches upgraded booking portal after 24 years: New beta website promises quicker, smoother and hassle-free train ticket bookings with 4 major upgrades
Article Text:
IRCTC launches new beta website for train ticket bookings



Key changes introduced in the new IRCTC website



Fewer disruptions in the booking process: The redesigned website eliminates irrelevant captchas, pop-ups, blinking images among other things which used to be a distraction during the booking process.

Easier check for seats: Customers can be able to check for seats available in various train categories easily during the search for trains.

Faster confirmation process for booking tickets: Fewer steps are involved in the booking process making it easy for customers to go through the entire booking process faster.

Faster repeat booking of tickets: Saved customer details makes it easy for people who frequently book tickets to make their bookings faster.

New IRCTC portal simplifies online ticket booking





Students contribute ideas for IRCTC website revamp



New IRCTC portal linked with upcoming railway technology upgrade



The Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) has rolled out the beta version of its redesigned website, introducing a cleaner, more user-friendly interface aimed at making online train ticket booking quicker and easier. The beta site went live at 9 pm on 15 July 2026, allowing users to explore the new design, test its features, and share feedback before the full public launch.The updated website includes several improvements to simplify the booking process. These include a less cluttered interface, clearer visibility of seat availability, a streamlined checkout experience, and other enhancements designed to help passengers book tickets more efficiently.The Ministry of Railways launched the beta version of the new IRCTC website on 15 July 2026. The updated portal is available through the IRCTC website, with a link also placed on the homepage of the existing platform.The website redesign comes more than two decades after IRCTC’s online ticketing platform was first introduced in 2002. The beta release is being tested before the full rollout, giving passengers an opportunity to experience the updated interface, share feedback, report issues, and suggest further improvements.The following are some of the modifications made on the new design to make the online ticket booking easier. The key changes involve:These changes have been made to simplify the website’s process of use by railway travelers.The new beta website has been developed with an emphasis on improving the overall user experience. Instead of adding more features, the redesign focuses on making existing functions easier to access.Passengers will notice a cleaner layout with fewer elements competing for attention. The changes are expected to be particularly useful during high-demand booking periods, when speed and ease of navigation are important factors for travellers.As reoported by PIB, the beta version will also help IRCTC collect feedback from users and identify areas where further refinements may be required before the final launch.Students from Malaviya National Institute of Technology (MNIT) were involved in suggesting improvements for the website’s design and user experience.Their recommendations were shared during an interaction with Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. The suggestions focused on making the portal more practical, easier to understand and better suited to the needs of everyday users.The ideas were later considered during the redesign process, leading to the development of the beta version now available for public testing.The website update is part of a larger technology overhaul taking place within Indian Railways. Alongside the IRCTC redesign, the Passenger Reservation Engine that supports railway ticketing systems is also being upgraded.The existing reservation system has been running for several years and requires extensive changes because it must continue handling ticket bookings during the upgrade process.Once the new reservation engine is ready, it will be integrated with the updated IRCTC platform. The Ministry of Railways has said that the complete version of the new portal is expected to become available in the coming weeks.The beta launch represents the first stage of this wider transformation, with passenger feedback expected to play a role in shaping future updates to the railway booking experience.
Article Summary: The Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) has rolled out the beta version of its redesigned website. The website update is part of a larger technology overhaul taking place within Indian Railways. The beta release is being tested before the full rollout, giving passengers an opportunity to experience the updated interface, report issues, and suggest further improvements.

Article Title: China ‘listens’ to Elon Musk, tells tech companies, make sure right away that: Chinese need to stop …
Article Text:
AI chatbot romance

‘AI lover’ trend booming



Threat to fertility and birthrates



The Chinese government has launched a crackdown on virtual romance, driven by an urgent demographic mission – it wants its citizens to stop dating artificial intelligence (AI) and start having human babies. China officially enacted rules that completely forbid AI chatbots designed for companionship from encouraging “emotional reliance” among users, as per a report by The Wall Street Journal. The decision sits squarely alongside Elon Musk’s repeated warnings about population collapse threatening the future of civilisation.The report said that China’s population shrank in 2025 for the fourth straight year, to 1.405 billion, and its birthrate fell to a record low. Further, this comes as US lawmakers are nudging companies to mental health warnings when talking with machines. The report said that the regulations hit the country’s biggest tech empires: Alibaba and TikTok's parent company, ByteDance, scrambled to inform users that multiple popular chatbot features would be disabled.The decision suggests a growing trend that highly sophisticated AI companions are beginning to replace real-world human interactions.US states like California and New York enacted laws requiring bots to remind users every three hours that they are not human.Beijing’s new laws explicitly ban any virtual relationships with minors. Furthermore, AI platforms are now legally required to secretly monitor conversations and immediately alert a user’s emergency human contact if they detect a severe emotional crisis.“They don’t like the idea of a large portion of their population being in deep emotional relationships with chatbots that could take them out of the marriage market,” explained Matt Sheehan, a researcher who studies Chinese AI at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. Sheehan warned that unchecked digital intimacy could lead to “addiction, dependency, and a whole bunch of other social ills.”The policy shift aligns with the government’s “AI Safety Governance Framework.” In official regulatory documents, Beijing warned that unchecked AI may dangerously destabilize society by “transforming traditional views on employment, fertility and education.”AI boyfriends and girlfriends are actively making the problem worse by keeping young people isolated, the report noted.“They want to encourage people to be in actual, real-world relationships. Could we imagine a future where, three or four years from now, 15 million Chinese women say that their partner is a chatbot, and therefore they’re not having kids?,” Sheehan said.Moving forward, all companion software must pass a regulatory evaluation before being offered to the public, giving the state authority to shut down any AI system deemed to be too emotionally engaging.
Article Summary: China has banned AI chatbots from encouraging ‘emotional reliance’ among users. China’s population shrank in 2025 for the fourth straight year, and its birthrate fell to a record low. The decision suggests a growing trend that highly sophisticated AI companions are beginning to replace real-world human interactions.

Article Title: Canadian man noticed a strange hole on Google Maps while planning a camping trip, and it turned out to be a 390-million-year-old meteor crater
Article Text:
PC: AI Generated

How a Google Maps search led to the discovery of a 390-million-year-old meteor crater

PC: AI Generated

Scientists travelled through remote Quebec to confirm the meteor crater

Naming the crater and trusting the gut feeling

Sometimes, you don't need to be a professional scientist to find something that changes our understanding of the world. This is exactly what happened to a Canadian man named Joël Lapointe. While he was sitting at his computer using Google Maps to plan a camping holiday in the Quebec region of Canada, he noticed something very strange.He saw a huge, circular pit in the ground that didn’t look like the rest of the forest. Because he was curious, he shared what he found with experts, and it turned out he had discovered a meteor crater. This giant hole in the ground was made when a massive rock from space crashed into Earth about 390 million years ago. To give you an idea of how big it is, the crater is 25 kilometres wide, which is much larger than most cities.After Joël shared his find, a team of four researchers decided they had to go and see it with their own eyes. In 2025, they set out on a mission to the remote area, which is about 100 kilometres north of a small place called Magpie. The group was led by Gordon Osinski, a professor who spends his life studying the rocks of different planets, and Jérôme Gattacceca, a rock expert from France.They were joined by two other scientists.Getting to the site was one of the hardest things the team had ever done. Professor Osinski has travelled all over the world, but he said the land here was very rough and covered in thick bushes and trees. It was so hard to reach that the small plane bringing them in couldn’t even land on the shore. Instead, the plane had to stop in the water about 50 metres away from the land as reported by CBC News. This meant the scientists had to jump into the water and wade to the shore while carrying all of their heavy gear. They spent five days exploring the area, taking many photos and picking up rock samples to bring back to their labs for testing.To be sure that a hole in the ground is actually a crater from space, scientists look for very specific clues that only a violent crash can leave behind. On their trip, the team found giant cliffs made of what they call "impact melt rock". Professor Osinski explained that when a big enough space rock hits the ground at a very high speed, it creates so much heat and pressure that it can turn tens of cubic kilometres of the Earth's surface into liquid. When this liquid cools down, it turns back into a special kind of solid rock that proved a meteor had hit that exact spot.They also looked for shatter cones, which are special marks in the rock that look like tiny fans or the feathers on a bird. These patterns are only made when a massive shockwave from a space crash travels through the ground. Finding these rocks and feather-like patterns confirmed that Joël Lapointe’s "unusual pit" was actually the site of a huge explosion from the very distant past. The discovery is so important to the scientific world that the researchers are getting ready to talk about it at a huge global conference next month, where experts from many different countries will come to hear the story.The new crater has been given a special name: Uhackatik. This name was chosen after the scientists talked with the Innu Council of Ekuanitshit, who are the local people who have lived in that part of Canada for a very long time. Joël Lapointe was very happy to hear that his find was real and that it was given a name that respects the local culture. He told Radio-Canada that he was very excited because "it's not every day that an ordinary person finds a 390-million-year-old crater", as reported by CBC News.
Article Summary: Scientists travelled through remote Quebec to confirm the meteor crater. The crater was made when a massive rock from space crashed into Earth about 390 million years ago. The new crater has been given a special name: Uhackatik. This name was chosen after the scientists talked with the Innu Council of Ekuanitshit.

Article Title: Quote of the day by former Google CEO Larry Page: "If you're not doing some things that are crazy, then…" - unconventional lesson on innovation, ambition and why the biggest ideas often sound impossib
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Larry Page (AI-generated image)

Quote of the day by Larry Page

"If you're not doing some things that are crazy, then you're doing the wrong things"

What is the meaning behind Larry Page’s quote

Where did Larry Page actually said this

Why unconventional ideas produce the biggest shifts

Why bold and reckless are not the same thing

Why failure has to be an accepted part of the process

Other famous quotes by Larry Page

"Always deliver more than expected."

"You never lose a dream; it just incubates as a hobby."

"Lots of companies don't succeed over time. What do they fundamentally do wrong? They usually miss the future."

"Almost everyone who has had an idea that's somewhat revolutionary or wildly successful was first told they're insane."

Why this still matters today

Most ideas that eventually changed everyday life sounded slightly ridiculous the first time anyone heard them. Larry Page built an entire approach to running Google around that observation. "If you're not doing some things that are crazy, then you're doing the wrong things," he said. He was not arguing that every strange idea has merit. He was arguing that playing it safe, doing only what already looks sensible, rarely produces anything genuinely new. Coming from someone who spent years directing Google's research into projects with no guaranteed payoff, driverless cars among them, the line reads less like a slogan and more like a description of how he actually chose to run the company, and what he expected everyone working under him to try attempting as well."Crazy" here does not mean reckless. It means ambitious enough to look implausible before it works, far ahead of existing technology, or built on an assumption nobody else had questioned yet. Page's point is that a person who only pursues what already looks achievable will get steady, incremental progress at best, never the kind of change that actually shifts an entire industry.Page said this in a January 2013 interview with Wired's Steven Levy, titled "Google's Larry Page On Why Moon Shots Matter."In that same conversation, he used Gmail as a concrete example, a product Google built while still known purely as a search company, offering users a hundred times more storage than anyone else provided at the time. That leap, he argued, would never have happened if Google had simply focused on incremental improvements to what it already did well.He also made a sharper point in the same interview about why large companies tend to decay slowly, arguing that most keep doing roughly what they did before, with only minor changes, because working on something guaranteed not to fail feels safer than working on something genuinely new.Systems that already work tend to attract habits and comfort around them, which is exactly why something unfamiliar often meets resistance regardless of its merit. The internet, search engines and smartphones all reshaped daily life, and each looked far less obviously important in its earliest form than it does in hindsight. Someone focused entirely on what was already popular at the time would have missed all three.None of this is an argument for abandoning judgement. A bold idea still needs real planning and honest testing, and ambition without any grounding in reality tips quickly into recklessness rather than innovation. The distinction that matters is whether an idea is being pursued through actual experimentation, or simply pursued because it sounds exciting.Attempting something new means accepting that it might not work, and Page's own approach treated that risk as necessary rather than something to avoid. If every idea needed a guarantee of success before anyone would try it, very little that is genuinely new would ever get built in the first place.Fields like artificial intelligence and biotechnology are still full of ideas that sound distant or unrealistic today, the same way search engines and smartphones once did. Page's quote does not offer a formula for spotting which of them will actually work. It offers a mindset instead, treating unfamiliarity as a reason to look closer rather than a reason to dismiss something outright.
Article Summary: Larry Page's quote of the day: "If you're not doing some things that are crazy, then you're doing the wrong things" Page was arguing that playing it safe, doing only what already looks sensible, rarely produces anything genuinely new. Page said this in a January 2013 interview with Wired's Steven Levy.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Marcus Aurelius that ‘inspired’ Elon Musk: ‘You have power over your mind, not outside events; realise this, and you will find strength’
Article Text:
Quote of the Day by Marcus Aurelius



What Marcus Aurelius' quote means



How Marcus Aurelius has inspired Elon Musk



A message reflected in history



A simple takeaway



Some quotes travel through centuries and arrive in the present moment feeling more relevant than when they were first written. This is one of them. Marcus Aurelius, the Roman Emperor who ruled from 161 to 180 AD and whose private journal of Stoic reflections has survived nearly two thousand years to become one of the most widely read works of philosophy in the world, wrote with a directness that cuts through the noise of any era. The quote is not comfort. It is instruction. And it has found a new generation of admirers, including some of the most powerful figures in contemporary business and technology."You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realise this, and you will find strength."At its core, the quote is drawing the most important distinction in Stoic philosophy: the line between what is within your control and what is not. Marcus Aurelius is not asking you to become indifferent to the world around you. He is asking you to be precise about where your agency actually begins and ends. The markets, the weather, other people's opinions, the decisions of competitors, the arc of geopolitical events — none of these belong to you. Your perception of them, your response to them, the meaning you assign to them — those do.The word "realise" is doing important work in the quote. It suggests that this is not an insight that arrives automatically.It has to be reached, understood, and then acted upon. The strength Aurelius promises is not physical and not external. It is the particular kind of steadiness that comes from no longer expending energy on things that were never yours to control in the first place.For a man who governed the most powerful empire in the world while simultaneously managing military campaigns, political intrigue, plague, and personal loss, this was not abstract philosophy. It was the operating principle of a life conducted under extraordinary pressure. The Meditations, from which this quote is drawn, were never intended for publication. They were private notes written to himself, reminders of how to behave when the circumstances around him were at their most difficult. That context makes the clarity of the writing all the more striking.Tesla CEO Elon Musk has always been vocal about his admiration for the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius. The Stoic leader has occupies a special place in how Musk thinks about leadership under pressure. In a now-widely-referenced tweet, Musk wrote: "I wonder if Marcus Aurelius could have done more to carry Rome to greater heights or whether that was as good a job as could have been done," a reflection that reveals less about Roman history and more about how Musk reads leadership, as a question of what was genuinely possible given the constraints at hand rather than an idealised standard measured against perfect conditions.For someone like Musk, who has built and also simultaneously managed multiple companies, each operating in conditions of extreme uncertainty and public scrutiny, the Stoic framework offers something that conventional motivational thinking does not: a philosophy built specifically for people whose responsibilities exceed their ability to control outcomes. The Stoic focus on internal disciple rather than on external validation which can also be seen in the decision of Elon Musk. SpaceX CEO has always described in interviews that pressing forward on SpaceX when the company's first three rockets failed, or continuing to invest in Tesla when the company was weeks from bankruptcy in 2008. In both cases, the only available leverage was the mind and the decisions it made.Not only this, on may occasions, Musk has shared messages from the Meditations on social media and cited Stoicism more broadly as a philosophical framework he returns to, suggesting that his engagement with Aurelius is less celebrity endorsement and more genuine intellectual habit.What makes Marcus Aurelius unusual among historical figures is that his philosophical commitments were tested publicly and at scale throughout his reign. He ruled during the Antonine Plague, one of the most devastating pandemics the ancient world experienced. He spent much of his time as emperor on military campaigns he had no appetite for, conducting them with discipline and effectiveness while continuing to write philosophical reflections at night. He lost multiple children. He governed an empire whose decline he could likely sense but could not reverse.And through all of it, the Meditations reveal a man practising exactly what this quote instructs: returning his attention to what was within his control, his judgement, his character, his effort, and finding in that return not resignation but strength.This quote by Marcus Aurelius is very useful but not as an instruction to disengage from the world, but as a redirect. The quotes highlights that when something outside of your control is absorbing disproportionate energy, Aurelius is suggesting to move towards the only productive place. Move that energy back into the decisions, habits, and responses that are genuinely yours. That is as practical an insight in 2026 as it was in second-century Rome, which is perhaps the most convincing argument for why it has lasted this long.
Article Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has always been vocal about his admiration for the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius. The Stoic leader has occupies a special place in how Musk thinks about leadership under pressure. Musk has shared messages from the Meditations on social media and cited Stoicism.

Article Title: After 20 patients in trials, as Elon Musk's Neuralink awaits FDA approval; China completes world’s first commercial brain-computer interface implant
Article Text:
China brain-computer interface: Commercial brain chip implanted after approval



China and Neuralink compete in brain chip technology

China has completed what it says is the world's first commercial implantation of an invasive brain-computer interface (BCI), marking a major milestone in its effort to compete with Elon Musk 's Neuralink. The procedure comes as Neuralink continues human trials in the United States but is still awaiting full approval from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for commercial use. As reported by South China Morning Post, Chinese doctors implanted a coin-sized brain chip in a patient with a spinal cord injury, making the device the first invasive BCI approved for commercial use rather than being limited to research or clinical trials.According to the Science and Technology Commission of Shanghai Municipality, the surgery was performed on Monday at Huashan Hospital. The patient had impaired hand movement following a spinal cord injury caused by a car accident 10 years ago.The implanted device, called NEO, was developed by Shanghai-based startup Neuracle Medical Technology. The company said the chip is placed on the outer surface of the brain without penetrating brain tissue. It reads neural signals and converts them into hand movements to help patients regain mobility.Officials said the patient recovered well after the operation, with stable vital signs and high-quality brain signals recorded during the procedure.The NEO device received approval from China's National Medical Products Administration on March 13, becoming the world's first commercially approved invasive brain-computer interface. Since then, the company has started production, introduced the device to hospitals, screened patients and secured inclusion in local commercial health insurance.The latest development highlights China's efforts to become a global leader in brain-computer interface technology. The country has identified BCIs as a strategic future industry and aims to develop two or three globally competitive companies by 2030.Meanwhile, Elon Musk's Neuralink has enrolled more than 20 patients in clinical trials for its first brain-computer interface product, Telepathy. However, Neuralink has not yet received full commercial approval from the U.S. FDA, meaning its technology remains in the clinical trial stage rather than being available for commercial use.
Article Summary: Chinese doctors implanted a coin-sized brain chip in a patient with a spinal cord injury, making the device the first invasive BCI approved for commercial use. The procedure comes as Neuralink continues human trials in the United States but is still awaiting full approval from the US Food and Drug Administration.

Article Title: Why and how OpenAI killing Atlas in less than a year does not mean AI browsers are dead, it actually means …
Article Text:
Chrome is not just a browser

AI browsers are entering their second phase

How OpenAI rivals are betting differently



The browser itself may disappear

Atlas is dead. The AI browser race may just be getting started. Less than nine months after launching ChatGPT Atlas, OpenAI has decided to kill it. At first glance, that sounds like a retreat. In reality, it is probably the clearest sign yet that the future of AI-powered browsing will not be about convincing people to abandon Google Chrome, Apple Safari or Microsoft Edge. It will be about making those browsers almost invisible.OpenAI announced last week that Atlas will be shut down, with its browser intelligence folded into ChatGPT's desktop app and a Chrome extension. Instead of asking users to switch browsers, ChatGPT will now travel with them wherever they browse. That strategic pivot says as much about browsers as it does about artificial intelligence.Every technology company has, at some point, believed it could build a better browser. Microsoft tried repeatedly. Mozilla fought the battle for years. Arc won acclaim among enthusiasts but remained a niche product. Even OpenAI, backed by one of the world's fastest-growing AI platforms, could not persuade enough users to change their default browser.The reason is simple. Browsers are among the stickiest products in technology. People's passwords, bookmarks, extensions, browsing history, autofill information and workplace policies are deeply embedded inside Chrome, Safari and Edge. Convincing someone to change browsers is far harder than convincing them to download another AI chatbot.Atlas discovered that reality quickly. Instead of continuing an expensive battle against entrenched incumbents, OpenAI appears to have concluded that AI is the feature users want, not necessarily another browser window.That does not mean AI browsers have failed. Quite the opposite. The first phase was about proving that AI could browse alongside users — summarise pages, answer questions, rewrite text and automate repetitive tasks. The second phase is about deciding where those capabilities should live. OpenAI's answer is: Everywhere.Rather than maintaining a standalone browser, the company is distributing Atlas' agentic capabilities across ChatGPT's desktop application, a Chrome extension and cloud-based browser agents capable of logging into websites, downloading files and completing multi-step tasks.The browser becomes infrastructure rather than the product.OpenAI's rivals are making different calculations. Perplexity continues to push Comet, betting that users are willing to adopt a dedicated AI browser built around search, research and persistent assistance. The Browser Company has effectively abandoned Arc in favour of Dia, an AI-first browser where the assistant sits directly inside the address bar rather than beside the webpage.Meanwhile, established browser makers are taking a more incremental route. Google is steadily weaving Gemini deeper into Chrome. Microsoft continues expanding Copilot inside Edge. Opera, Brave and Firefox have all integrated AI assistants without asking users to fundamentally change how they browse.That means the competition is no longer between browsers. It is increasingly between AI assistants. The real race is for context. Search engines competed to answer questions. Similarly, AI browsers compete to understand context.The winner will not necessarily have the smartest language model. It will be the assistant that knows what document you're reading, which tab you're working in, which email you're replying to, which spreadsheet you're editing and what task you're trying to finish. And that explains OpenAI's move.Instead of limiting Atlas to webpages, ChatGPT can now carry context across desktop applications, browser tabs and cloud agents. It becomes a continuous workspace rather than a browser. In other words, OpenAI has stopped thinking about browsing as a destination. It is treating it as just another source of context. But the hardest problems remain.This shift also magnifies the industry's biggest challenges. AI assistants increasingly require permission to read webpages, emails, calendars, documents and even browser history to deliver useful answers. That creates obvious questions around privacy, enterprise security and data governance.Agentic browsers also introduce entirely new attack surfaces. Researchers have already warned about prompt-injection attacks, where malicious webpages manipulate AI assistants into taking unintended actions. The more authority these assistants receive—logging into websites, making purchases or filling forms—the higher the security stakes become. For enterprise customers, governance may become a bigger differentiator than raw model quality.The biggest takeaway from Atlas' shutdown is not that AI browsers are dying. It is that the browser is becoming less important. Over the next few years, users are unlikely to care whether an AI assistant runs inside Chrome, Safari, Edge or something entirely new.They will care whether it can plan a holiday, compare insurance policies, analyse a 200-page report, book meetings, negotiate forms and complete work across dozens of websites without constant supervision. The browser becomes the operating layer.The AI becomes the interface. That may ultimately be why Atlas disappeared so quickly. OpenAI realised it did not need to win the browser wars to win the much larger battle for how people interact with the web. The first generation of AI browsers tried to replace Chrome. The next generation may simply make users forget which browser they are using.
Article Summary: OpenAI announced last week that Atlas will be shut down, with its browser intelligence folded into ChatGPT's desktop app and a Chrome extension. The future of AI-powered browsing will not be about convincing people to abandon Google Chrome, Apple Safari or Microsoft Edge. It will be about making those browsers almost invisible.

Article Title: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada's notice: Government of Canada is pausing the intake of new applications under ...
Article Text:
Flag of Canada

Family reunification still a priority



Managing Demand



Canada warns citizens of Immigration marriage fraud



The Government of Canada announced that it is pausing new applications under the Parents and Grandparents Program (PGP) as part of efforts to maintain a sustainable immigration system. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) confirmed that while new applications will not be accepted, existing files will continue to be processed, with plans to approve up to approve up to 15,000 people for permanent residence in 2026 in line with the 2026–2028 Immigration Levels Plan. “Canada is taking steps to maintain a well‑managed, sustainable immigration system that works for newcomers and Canadians alike. As part of these efforts, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) is pausing the intake of new applications under the Parents and Grandparents Program (PGP Program). We will continue to process existing applications and plan to approve up to 15,000 people for permanent residence through the PGP Program in 2026, in line with the 2026–2028 Immigration Levels Plan. This approach will help reduce processing times and improve predictability for families,” reads the press release.IRCC also stressed on the point that family reunification is still a central pillar of Canada’s Immigration framework. Parents and grandparents can continue to visit their families through the super visa, which allows stays of up to five years at a time and multiple entries for up to ten years. Recent changes have made the super visa more accessible by easing income and health insurance requirements. “Parents and grandparents continue to be able to visit their children and grandchildren in Canada through the super visa, which allows them to visit their children or grandchildren for 5 years at a time and provides multiple entries to Canada for up to 10 years,” added the government.Interest in the PGP Program continues to exceed available spaces under the immigration levels plan. To manage this demand responsibly, IRCC stated it will not accept new interest-to-sponsor forms or invite potential sponsors to apply until further notice. By pausing intake, Canada aims to reduce processing times and improve predictability for families, ensuring the immigration system remains well-managed and sustainable for newcomers and Canadians alike.Recently, Canada’s immigration authority has issued a fresh advisory urging citizens to be cautious about marriage fraud when sponsoring a spouse or partner for immigration.The warning, shared on X by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), highlights red flags that could indicate fraudulent intent. Canada's federal immigration authority is urging citizens and permanent residents to slow down before walking down the aisle with someone they plan to sponsor for immigration, warning that marriage fraud remains a serious and growing problem that can have lasting legal and financial consequences for the person being deceived. “Think carefully before marrying someone and sponsoring them to come to Canada, especially if: you’ve just met they want to get married quickly they’ve been married or in a common-law relationship many times before they haven’t shared much information about their background or family,” reads the post shared by IRCC.IRCC advised Canadians to think carefully before marrying someone and sponsoring them to come to Canada, especially if:* Quick marriage: The person wants to marry soon after meeting.* Multiple past relationships: They have been married or in common‑law partnerships many times before.* Lack of background details: They avoid sharing information about their family or personal history.* Recent acquaintance: You have only just met them.
Article Summary: The Government of Canada announced that it is pausing new applications under the Parents and Grandparents Program (PGP) as part of efforts to maintain a sustainable immigration system. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) confirmed that while new applications will not be accepted, existing files will continue to be processed. IRCC advised Canadians to think carefully before marrying someone and sponsoring them to come to Canada.

Article Title: Microsoft to sales team on how to make customers 'dump' OpenAI and Anthropic: Tell them everyone else is selling ...

Article Title: Judge blocks Trump government's visa restrictions for foreign researchers, trust-and-safety professionals including CEO of the US-based ...
Article Text:
What the judge said about Trump visa policy

A US federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from enforcing an immigration policy that could deny visas or deport foreign researchers and trust-and-safety professionals working on misinformation, disinformation and online hate speech. Chief US District Judge James Boasberg ruled that the policy likely violates the free speech protections of the US Constitution's First Amendment. The decision also affects people linked to US-based organisations, including Center for Countering Digital Hate (CCDH) CEO Imran Ahmed, who was among those previously targeted under the administration's visa restrictions.For those unaware, the State Department imposed visa bans on five Europeans, including Imran Ahmed, the British CEO of the U.S.-based Center for Countering Digital Hate, and Clare Melford, co-founder of the Global Disinformation Index in December last year. As per the lawsuit, both organisations are members of the Coalition for Independent Technology Research.The lawsuit was originally filed by the Coalition for Independent Technology Research, which argued that the US State Department had launched a broad campaign against researchers and advocates working on content moderation and combating online misinformation.The State Department, the court order said, announced a policy targeting foreign nationals in 2025 that is said to be complicit in censoring Americans. “What began as a visa-restriction policy later expanded, according to Plaintiff Coalition for Independent Technology Research, into a broader campaign against noncitizens who work on misinformation, disinformation, fact checking, content moderation, compliance, and trust and safety,” the order stated.Judge Boasberg agreed that the policy likely placed foreign nationals at risk because of their work. He said non-citizens, including researchers working with the coalition, "could reasonably understand the policy to place their immigration status at risk — not because they wield foreign sovereign power or facilitate its censorship, but simply because they work in content moderation."The judge said the administration appeared to be treating research and advocacy supporting stronger content moderation as grounds for visa denials, exclusion or deportation, likely violating First Amendment protections.Carrie DeCell, a lawyer representing the coalition through the Knight First Amendment Institute at Columbia University, welcomed the ruling.“This policy punishes researchers for work the public needs and the First Amendment protects,” DeCell said. “We’re glad the court recognized the serious constitutional harms this policy is already causing and blocked the government from enforcing it while the case proceeds”.
Article Summary: A US federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from enforcing an immigration policy that could deny visas or deport foreign researchers. Chief US District Judge James Boasberg ruled that the policy likely violates the free speech protections of the US Constitution. The decision also affects people linked to US-based organisations, including Center for Countering Digital Hate CEO Imran Ahmed.

Article Title: AI Appreciation Day 2026: Celebrating true value of AI focusing on innovation, safety and growth of humanity
Article Text:
Representative Photo (AP Photo/Manuel Balce Ceneta)

Srinivas Rao, Managing Director, Infrastructure Solutions Group, Lenovo India

Arnold Su, Vice President of Consumer & Gaming PC, Asus India

Shailesh Singla, vice president, Cloud Applications, Oracle India

Mayank Baid, Regional Vice President, India & South Asia,

Cloudera

Atul Ahuja, Area Vice President and General Manager, Elastic India

Nitin Golani, CEO, UNIVO Education

Amit Shrivastav, Global Head AI GTM & Director Product Management at Kellton Tech

Navin Bishnoi, VP and India Country Manager

Celebrated annually on July 16, AI Appreciation Day 2026 marks a profound shift in how humanity interacts with artificial intelligence. First time observed in the year 2021 to honor technological achievements while fostering critical discussions around ethics and regulation, the day has evolved from a niche tech milestone into a global checkpoint for society. The core theme of AI Appreciation Day 2026 extends far beyond celebrating raw computational capability. The 2026 conversation focuses on governance, transparency, and trust. As agentic AI systems independently execute complex tasks, the tech community, policymakers, and the public are using this day to champion responsible innovation. AI Appreciation Day serves as a reminder that the true value of artificial intelligence is defined not just by what the technology can achieve, but by how safely, ethically, and equitably it serves humanity.In 2026, AI is no longer viewed merely as a futuristic novelty or a basic productivity tool for writing and analyzing data. Instead, it has become our default infrastructure -- quietly operating behind the scenes to power autonomous workflows, assist medical diagnostics, predict environmental patterns, and defend critical networks against machine-speed cybersecurity threats.“AI adoption has clearly moved beyond experimentation to real business deployment, but the next phase will be defined by how effectively organizations scale it.Today, the challenge is no longer access to AI, but aligning architecture, governance, and cost models to deliver sustained value. As enterprises increasingly explore agentic and physical AI, success will depend on placing the right workloads on the right infrastructure across cloud, edge, and on-premises, while building strong governance frameworks from the outset. The organizations that will lead are not the fastest adopters, but those that approach AI with clarity on economics, execution, and long-term resilience.”“The most meaningful AI won't be the features users actively seek out, but the intelligence working quietly in the background, helping people create faster, collaborate more effectively, safeguard their privacy, and get more from their devices with less effort. As AI becomes an integral part of personal computing, the responsibility for technology companies is not just to innovate, but to deliver AI experiences that are intuitive, reliable, transparent, and built on trust. "On AI Appreciation Day, it's worth reflecting on how far we've come. Not long ago, organizations were experimenting with AI through pilots and isolated use cases. Today, the conversation has shifted to delivering meaningful business outcomes at scale. The real promise of AI lies in turning everyday work into extraordinary business outcomes. The most impactful AI often works behind the scenes—it is embedded into the applications and workflows people use every day, whether it's helping finance teams forecast with greater confidence, HR leaders make better talent decisions, or supply chains respond faster to change. As AI becomes native to enterprise applications, it's doing more than automating tasks. It's helping people make smarter decisions, work more efficiently, and focus on higher-value work. The real value of AI is not in isolated capabilities, but in making everyday work more intelligent across the enterprise. Ultimately, AI's greatest impact will come from embedding intelligence into the everyday work of every team, enabling organizations to innovate faster and achieve better business outcomes.“AI has evolved from a promising technology into a strategic business priority, reshaping how organizations drive competitive differentiation, efficiency, and growth. As enterprises move from pilots to production, success increasingly depends not just on deploying the right models, but on ensuring access to trusted, governed data that serves as its foundation. Today, the focus is shifting toward building AI that is sustainable, secure, and accountable across complex environments. Organizations that can combine trusted data with strong governance, transparency, and control will be best positioned to move beyond experimentation and deliver meaningful business outcomes while building long-term confidence in AI.”"Decades of enterprise knowledge sit locked inside applications, business systems and workflows, leaving every organisation with information that is valuable but rarely connected in ways AI can readily use. Deloitte's State of AI in the Enterprise report puts a number to where India stands: nearly 40 per cent of Indian organisations already report significant or full-scale AI adoption, and 94 per cent expect AI investment to increase over the next year. The momentum is real, but investment alone does not produce reliable AI outcomes. Attention is increasingly turning to the quality of enterprise data and the ability to retrieve it efficiently, because AI can only work with the information it can access. Retrieval brings together information spread across the enterprise, giving AI the context it needs to understand relationships, reason more accurately and produce reliable outcomes."AI is rapidly becoming the defining technology of our time, transforming industries, redefining business models, and reshaping the future of work. Its impact extends far beyond automation. It is enabling organizations to make smarter decisions, enhance productivity, accelerate innovation, and deliver more personalized experiences at an unprecedented scale. As AI continues to evolve, the real opportunity lies not just in adopting the technology but in integrating it responsibly to create sustainable value for businesses and society.The hardest problem in AI is no longer capability; it is trust. As models grow more autonomous, the organizations that win will be those that pair ambition with accountability. Ethical AI cannot be a compliance checkbox bolted on after deployment; it must be designed into the architecture from the first line of code. Governance, transparency, and meaningful human oversight are not brakes on innovation; they are what make innovation durable. An AI decision that cannot be explained, audited, or overruled is a liability waiting to surface. The future workplace will be one where humans and intelligent agents collaborate, but where judgment, values, and ultimate responsibility remain human. We must build systems that are powerful enough to transform industries and principled enough to deserve our confidence. The measure of mature AI is not how much it can do alone, but how well it earns the trust of the people it serves.The rapid advancement of AI has fundamentally changed the way data moves through modern computing infrastructure. Connectivity is emerging as a critical determinant of performance, efficiency and innovation. The industry is entering a phase where new breakthroughs will not depend primarily on more powerful compute resources, but on the ability to deliver high-bandwidth, low-latency data communication across thousands of accelerators and increasingly distributed data center environments. Advances in optical connectivity and networking will play a pivotal role in the next generation of AI infrastructure and unlocking new possibilities for AI at scale. AI Appreciation Day is a reminder that behind every breakthrough are teams solving complex engineering problems, from moving data efficiently to designing systems that can scale reliably. The real appreciation should extend to building the foundations that make AI usable in the real world.
Article Summary: AI Appreciation Day 2026 marks a profound shift in how humanity interacts with artificial intelligence. The day has evolved from a niche tech milestone into a global checkpoint for society. The challenge is no longer access to AI, but aligning architecture, governance, and cost models to deliver sustained value.

Article Title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon 'agrees' Anthropic Mythos AI model is dangerous; says: You are giving ballistic ⁠missiles to ...
Article Text:
Anthropic released Mythos to a select group that included JPMorgan

JPMorgan’s cybersecurity push

JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon has raised some sharp conversations about Anthropic’s powerful AI model Mythos, calling the risks a ‘real issue’ that US authorities are monitoring. According to a report by Reuters, speaking at Senator Dave McCormick’s Pennsylvania Defense and Innovation Summit, Dimon said that the access to advanced AY must be tightly controlled. “You’re giving ballistic missiles to individuals with Mythos,” he warned, underscoring fears that such technology could be misused if not properly safeguarded. In a recent interview with CNBC, Dimon agreed that AI is making cyber threats more severe. Dimon revealed that JPMorgan was testing Anthropic’s latest AU model Mythos, which has already demonstrated its ability to uncover thousands of vulnerabilities in corporate software. Dimon told analysts, “AI’s made it worse, it’s made it harder. It does create additional vulnerabilities, and maybe down the road, better ways to strengthen yourself too.”When asked about Mythos, Dimon pointed to Anthropic’s own warnings about the tool’s capabilities. “It shows a lot more vulnerabilities need to be fixed,” he said, acknowledging both the risks and potential benefits of deploying advanced AI in cybersecurity.In April this year, Anthropic released Mythos to a select group which also included JPMorgan. The model quickly gained attention for its ability to identify cybersecurity vulnerabilities, helping firms uncover and fix weaknesses more efficiently. But in June, the US government ordered Anthropic to restrict access to its top AI models Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for foreign nationals, citing national security concerns. Anthropic later implemented new safeguards, leading Washington to lift the restrictions.As the world’s largest bank by market capitalization, JPMorgan has long invested heavily in cybersecurity. Dimon said the bank employs top experts and maintains constant coordination with government agencies. “We spend a lot of money. We’ve got top experts. We’re in constant contact with the government. It’s a full-time job, and we’re doing it all the time,” he noted.Still, Dimon warned that risks extend beyond any single institution due to the interconnected nature of the financial system. “Banks are attached to exchanges and all these other things that create other layers of risk,” he said. JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum echoed Dimon’s concerns, saying the industry has long recognised that AI can both expose vulnerabilities and be exploited in “attack mode” by bad actors. “These tools can make it easier to find vulnerabilities, but then also potentially be deployed by bad actors,” Barnum said.Dimon stressed that while advanced AI tools are important, traditional cybersecurity practices remain essential. “A lot of it is hygiene… how do you protect your data? How do you protect your networks, your routers, your hardware, changing your passcode? Doing all those things right dramatically reduces the risk,” he said.
Article Summary: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon has raised some sharp conversations about Anthropic’s powerful AI model Mythos. “You’re giving ballistic missiles to individuals with Mythos,” he warned, underscoring fears that such technology could be misused if not properly safeguarded.

Brown's exit comes as AWS continues to see strong growth from AI-related demand. Article Summary: Dave Brown, one of Amazon Web Services' longest-serving executives, is leaving the company after nearly 19 years.
